title: Adapters: the in-process bridge pattern
preamble:
# Adapters: the in-process bridge pattern

How an integrator writes an **adapter** — the glue
between an external system (MQTT broker, REST API,
camera detector, serial device, anything) and
libds's C API. Adapters run **in-process** with
libds and use its typed-callback surface; there is
no wire, no peer layer, no protobuf.

This doc describes the **mechanics** of building an
adapter against libds. The **contract** an adapter
promises to rule authors — the schemas it emits, the
services it offers, when it emits — lives in the
language tree at [LADP]. The two docs pair: LADP is what authors see;
NADP is what the adapter implementer wires up.

## What this is not

- Not the language-side adapter contract (schemas
  emitted, service shapes, declared filters). See
  LADP.
- Not specific to any one external system; each
  adapter has its own implementation tree.
- Not a code library — libds doesn't ship adapters.
  Each integrator builds the adapter that fits their
  deployment.
